answer.rationale: With the primary contract expiring in 14 days, no auto-renew, and the line already at 94% of committed volume with zero buffer, switching primary vendor now carries unacceptable delivery-risk exposure — onboarding a new supplier under this timeline is exactly the scenario where integration or ramp issues would breach committed volume. Memory_c2's positive switch outcome was under different conditions (no time pressure, existing buffer) and is a single archived success story that may not generalize; memory_c1 and memory_c6 support that incumbent renewal, including multi-year terms, has reliably preserved delivery stability and can still capture some cost benefit via term length even though price itself is closed this cycle. Renewing preserves supply continuity now, but does not satisfy the 18% cost mandate since the incumbent refused to reopen price — this gap must be explicitly flagged as unresolved and revisited next cycle via second-sourcing or vendor switch once there is time buffer to de-risk a transition. I verified c1 and c2 because they represent the two riskiest and most consequential inherited claims (stability of renewal vs. safety of switching) directly relevant to a decision made under a hard deadline with no slack.
